memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If after all this you will not listen to me, I will punish you for your
sins seven times over. I will break down your stubborn pride and make the
sky above you like iron and the ground beneath you like bronze'"
- Lev 26:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's warnings escalate, and the reason is revealing. The problem He
targets is named directly: stubborn pride. The discipline was aimed not
merely at behaviour but at the hard, unbending heart underneath it.

Notice the phrase "seven times over." This is not cold arithmetic. In
Scripture, seven often signals completeness. God is saying His response
to persistent rebellion would be thorough — not because He delights in
punishing, but because He is determined to break through a hardened
heart.

Dear reader, pride is the root sin, the one beneath all others. It was
pride that fell from heaven. It is pride that says, I will run my own
life, I do not need to listen, I know better than God. And pride is the
hardest thing in us to surrender.

The image of iron skies and bronze ground pictures a heaven that seems
closed and a life that yields nothing — the barrenness that stubbornness
finally produces.

God's word is consistent: He opposes the proud but shows favour to the
humble (Jas 4:6; 1 Pet 5:5). Notice that pride does not just fail to earn
God's help; it actively sets us against Him.

Here is the mercy hidden in the warning. God breaking our stubborn pride
is not cruelty — it is rescue. Pride is a prison, and He loves us too much
to leave us locked inside it.

Ask Him to do the humbling work now, gently, rather than requiring
something harder later.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where is stubborn pride ruling in my heart?
2. Am I resisting God in some area, insisting on my own way?
3. Will I let God humble me gently now rather than requiring more later?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, expose the pride in me that I cannot even see. Break my stubborn
heart gently, and give me the humility that receives Your grace. Amen.
